notes: Subject insert. Coin kinds are individuals (instance_of / subclass_of, with the catalogued chain instance_of o subclass_of ⊑ instance_of). 'Made without the Mint's authorization' is a firm class rule over the members of the kind. The two worlds only differ on the count of known specimens, so they carry no axioms; q2 and q3 count the members of a collection, tagged fol arithmetic in the record since 2026-10-31.

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): compares the count of known specimens with five

fol.notes: Coins are an uninterpreted sort with one constant per specimen the model knows (the five pedigrees); instance_of a kind is a Bool relation. Counting needs a closed world: the five are distinct and are all the known specimens (presuppositions). That the Corvell specimen is none of the five is part of the edit (the record's notes: a newly surfaced sixth). w1 stores the count as a figure (number_known), which the edit does not recompute; w2 stores the counting rule over the list (each named coin counted once, so the distinctness presupposition enters the count).

five_known.says: The Eliasberg, Olsen, Norweb, Walton and McDermott specimens are 1913 Liberty Head nickels. (stored list)

distinct_five.says: The five known specimens are five different coins. (closed world)

named_only.says: Every 1913 Liberty Head nickel the model knows of is one of the named coins. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(c, Implies(instance_of(c, nickel1913), Or(c == eliasberg, c == olsen, c == norweb, c == walton, c == mcdermott, c == corvell)))

edit: And(corvell != eliasberg, corvell != olsen, corvell != norweb, corvell != walton, corvell != mcdermott)
